Quamvis autem testimonium istud modo reddat conscientia, tamen in futuro extremo judicio clarius perhibebit. Tunc namque quilibet conscius erit sibi de propriis bonis ac malis. Ideirco subjungitur, in die quum judicabit Deus occulta hominum, id est in die judicii, quando aperientur conscientiarum libri, secundum evan[…]lium meum, id est secundum quod ego evangelizo ac prædico. Evangelium enim est Christi, tanquam auctoris ; Joannis vero, Matthæi, Lucæ, et Marci, tanquam scriptorum; Pauli autem et aliorum Apostolorum, tanquam prædicatorum. Quod vero mox subditur, per Jesum Christum, referri potest ad illud quod dictum est, Judicabit Deus, etc., quia per Christum hominem exercebitur illud judicium, ita quod ipse ut homo erit exsecutor judicii (Pater enim non judicat quemquam, sed judicium omne dedit Filio); vel ad illud quod dictum est, Secundum evangelium meum. Per Christum enim factum est evangelium Pauli, sicut superius ait : Per quem accepimus gratiam et apostolatum.
1.en: These, then, who by nature do the things of the law are a law to themselves: which the Apostle makes plain by the effect, namely by the witness of conscience. For it is added, [[2:15|their conscience bearing witness to them|testimonium reddente illis conscientia ipsorum]] of good or evil, the conscience which by the natural judgment of reason rejects evil and approves good: for it kicks back in a manner against a vicious work, and consents to a virtuous act; [[2:15|and their thoughts between themselves accusing or also defending one another|et inter se invicem cogitationum accusantium, aut etiam defendentium]]. In the manner of the Greeks he puts the genitive for the ablative, so that the sense is: their thoughts accusing one another, that is, the perverse thoughts which accuse the wicked, or also defending, that is, the good thoughts which excuse and defend the good: these thoughts, I say, bearing them witness of damnation or salvation, that is, to the Gentiles spoken of. These accusing and defending thoughts, that is, bad and good, are examined, judged and declared before the natural judgment-seat of man, as before a judge, by the first principles of action naturally implanted and known, such as that, [[Matt 7:12|whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you also to them|Quod tibi vis fieri, fac alteri]] [Denis gives the saying in the common form, "What you would have done to you, do to another"]. And although conscience bears this witness now, yet in the last judgment to come it will bear it more clearly. For then each one will be conscious to himself of his own good and evil. Therefore it is added, [[2:16|In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men|in die quum judicabit Deus occulta hominum]], that is, on the day of judgment, when the books of consciences will be opened, [[2:16|according to my gospel|secundum evangelium meum]], that is, according to what I preach as the gospel. For the Gospel is Christ's as its author; John's, Matthew's, Luke's and Mark's as its writers; and Paul's and the other Apostles' as its preachers. And what is added at once, [[2:16|by Jesus Christ|per Jesum Christum]], may be referred to what was said, *God shall judge*, etc., because that judgment will be carried out by Christ as man, so that he as man will be the executor of the judgment (for [[John 5:22|neither does the Father judge any man: but hath given all judgment to the Son|Pater enim non judicat quemquam, sed judicium omne dedit Filio]]); or to what was said, *according to my gospel*. For through Christ the gospel of Paul came about, as he said above: [[Rom 1:5|By whom we have received grace and apostleship|Per quem accepimus gratiam et apostolatum]].

1.t: Potest quoque ita exponi : Testimonium illis reddente conscientia ipsorum, id est conscientia operum; nec solum conscientia operum, sed et conscientia cogitationum inter se invicem accusantium aut defendentium, juxta sensum præhabitum. Dicit autem glossator, quod in die judicii cogitationes accusabunt animam vel defendent, non quæ tunc erunt, sed quæ nunc sunt in nobis : quarum quædam notæ atque signacula relinquuntur in corde nostro, velut in cera, quæ in occulto nunc pectoris posita, tunc revelari dicuntur per Christum. Sed contra ire huic videtur quod ait Anselmus, et alii Sancti, quod etiam certum est, scilicet quod in die judicii erit in reprobis conscientia urens atque remordens, in electis vero conscientia bonæ fiduciæ. Omnium enim opera cunctis patebunt. Sciendum ergo, quod cogitationes quæ nunc sunt, tunc accusabunt vel defendent per modum meriti sive demeriti. Cogitationes vero quæ tunc erunt, accusabunt aut defendent, non per modum meriti vel demeriti, quia non erit tunc locus merendi aut demerendi quum via sit finita, sed tanquam signa præteritorum meritorum aut demeritorum. Et sic glossator salvatur per distinctionem.
1.en: It may also be expounded thus: *their conscience bearing witness to them*, that is, the conscience of their works; and not only the conscience of works, but also the conscience of their thoughts accusing or defending one another, in the sense given before. And the glossator says that on the day of judgment the thoughts will accuse or defend the soul, not those that will be then, but those that are in us now: of which certain marks and seals are left in our heart, as in wax, which, laid up now in the hidden place of the breast, are said to be revealed then through Christ. But against this seems to go what Anselm and other saints say, which is also certain, namely that on the day of judgment there will be in the reprobate a conscience burning and gnawing, and in the elect a conscience of good confidence. For the works of all will be open to all. We must know, then, that the thoughts that are now will then accuse or defend by way of merit or demerit; but the thoughts that will be then will accuse or defend, not by way of merit or demerit, since there will then be no place for meriting or demeriting, the way being ended, but as signs of past merits or demerits. And so the glossator is saved by a distinction.

1.t: Consequenter Apostolus Judæos aggreditur, probans eos, quantum ad aliquid, deteriores gentilibus. Quo enim plura beneficia atque auxilia contra peccatum receperunt, eo gravius peccaverunt in eodem genere culpæ : quia quo status sublimior, eo ruina est major. Denique excellentia status Judæorum fuit in hoc, quod legem divinam, præcepta moralia, judicialia ac cærimonialia, diversaque alia gratiarum munera receperunt. Unde Moyses loquebatur : Quæ est alia gens sic inclyta, ut habeat cærimonias, justaque judicia, et universam legem, ut populus tuus, Israel? Ipsi vero ingrati Deo fuerunt. Propter quod Dominus conqueritur per Prophetam : Filios, inquiens, enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me. His ergo nunc ait Apostolus :
1.en: Next the Apostle attacks the Jews, proving them in some respect worse than the Gentiles. For the more benefits and helps against sin they received, the more grievously they sinned in the same kind of fault: since the higher the state, the greater the fall. Lastly, the excellence of the state of the Jews lay in this, that they received the divine law, the moral, judicial and ceremonial precepts, and various other gifts of grace. Hence Moses said: [[Deut 4:8|For what other nation is there so renowned that hath ceremonies, and just judgments, and all the law|Quæ est alia gens sic inclyta, ut habeat cærimonias, justaque judicia, et universam legem]], as thy people, Israel? But they were ungrateful to God. For which reason the Lord complains through the Prophet: [[Is 1:2|I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me|Filios, inquiens, enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me]] (he says). To these, then, the Apostle now says:

1.t: Si autem, id est quia, tu Judæus cognominaris a Juda patriarcha, qui inter fratres suos fortissimus erat, ut dicit Scriptura. Primo siquidem appellati sunt Hebræi ab Heber, in quo remansit lingua Hebraica, quæ ante constructionem turris Babylonicæ omnibus erat communis, juxta illud : Erat autem terra labii unius. Postmodum dicti sunt Israelitæ a Jacob, qui vocatus est Israel. Tertio dicti sunt Judæi a Juda. Hoc tamen nomine specialiter vocabantur duæ tribus. Nam Israel dictæ sunt aliæ decem tribus, a tempore separationis suæ a domo David. Et requiescis, id est persistis, in lege Mosaica, non evagando per diversos errores more gentilium, et gloriaris in Deo, id est in cognitione ipsius, et nosti voluntatem ejus ex doctrina legis ac Prophetarum, et probas, id est, approbas seu commendas, utiliora, id est perfectiora et viciniora saluti, instructus per legem, in qua diversi gradus perfectionum docentur; confidis, id est, præsumis et æstimas, te ipsum ducem esse cæcorum, id est tantæ perfectionis, ut aliis spiritualiter excæcatis possis viam virtutis ostendere, eosque in via Dei præcedere, atque ad rectum finem perducere; confidis quoque te lumen esse eorum qui in tenebris ignorantiæ sunt, id est tantæ gratiæ ac scientiæ, ut ignorantes valeas illustrare, eruditorem insipientium, id est divinorum cognitione carentium, scilicet infidelium, quos Judæi sæpe converterunt ad Deum, magistrum infantium, hoc est parvulorum seu imperfectorum, qui solidum cibum capere non valentes, expertes sunt sermonis justitiæ, habentem formam, id est perfectionem aliis exemplarem, scientiæ in agendis, et veritatis in lege, id est in credendis ac speculativis.
1.en: [[2:17|But if thou art called a Jew|Si autem tu Judæus cognominaris]], *if*, that is, since, from Juda the patriarch, who [[1 Par 5:2|was the strongest among his brethren|inter fratres suos fortissimus erat]], as Scripture says. For first they were called Hebrews from Heber[[Gen 10:21||]], in whom the Hebrew tongue remained, which before the building of the tower of Babel was common to all, according to that: [[Gen 11:1|And the earth was of one tongue|Erat autem terra labii unius]]. Afterwards they were called Israelites from Jacob, who was called Israel[[Gen 32:28||]][[Gen 35:10||]]. Thirdly they were called Jews from Juda. Yet by this name two tribes were called in a special way: for the other ten tribes were called Israel, from the time of their separation from the house of David[[3 Kings 12:19||]]. [[2:17|and restest|Et requiescis]], that is, abide, [[2:17|in the law|in lege]] of Moses, not wandering through various errors after the manner of the Gentiles, [[2:17|and makest thy boast of God|et gloriaris in Deo]], that is, in the knowledge of him, [[2:18|And knowest his will|et nosti voluntatem ejus]] from the teaching of the law and the Prophets, [[2:18|and approvest|et probas]], that is, commend, [[2:18|the more profitable things|utiliora]], that is, the more perfect and nearer to salvation, [[2:18|being instructed by the law|instructus per legem]], in which various degrees of perfection are taught; [[2:19|Art confident|confidis]], that is, presume and think, [[2:19|that thou thyself art a guide of the blind|te ipsum ducem esse cæcorum]], that is, of such perfection that you can show the way of virtue to others who are spiritually blinded, and go before them in the way of God, and lead them to the right end; you are confident also that you are [[2:19|a light of them that are in darkness|lumen … eorum qui in tenebris … sunt]] of ignorance, that is, of such grace and knowledge that you can enlighten the ignorant, [[2:20|An instructor of the foolish|eruditorem insipientium]], that is, of those lacking the knowledge of divine things, namely unbelievers, whom the Jews often converted to God, [[2:20|a teacher of infants|magistrum infantium]], that is, of little ones or the imperfect, who, not being able to take solid food, are unskilful in the word of justice[[Heb 5:12||]][[Heb 5:13||]], [[2:20|having the form|habentem formam]], that is, a perfection that is an example to others, [[2:20|of knowledge|scientiæ]] in what is to be done, [[2:20|and of truth in the law|et veritatis in lege]], that is, in what is to be believed and speculative matters.

1.t: Porro, quod subditur, interrogative, admirative et increpative intelligendum est. Qui ergo alium doces, te ipsum non doces? id est, quum alium docere præsumas, cur te ipsum non doces? Et mirum est quod te ipsum non doces; et male agis, eo quod te ipsum non doceas. Simili modo legenda sunt quæ sequuntur. Qui prædicas non furandum, furaris? Qui dicis non mœchandum, mœcharis? Commiserunt autem Judæi et spirituale furtum ac mœchationem, subtrahendo a lege sensum de Christo ac mysticum intellectum. Qui abominaris idola, id est idololatriæ cultum, sacrilegium facis, id est furtum atque abusum rei sacræ? Aliqua enim divino cultui deputata, propriis usibus applicabant Judæi, quia avarissimi erant sacerdotes, Scribæ ac Pharisæi. Nam divina præcepta suis superstitiosis traditionibus irrita fecerunt, ut Evangelium loquitur. Qui in lege, id est de legis acceptione, gloriaris, dicendo, Quanta audivimus et cognovimus ea; et, Non fecit taliter omni nationi; per prævaricationem legis Deum inhonoras, non exhibendo ei reverentiam debitam, obediendo mandatis ipsius? Nomen enim Dei per vos, id est occasione vestri, blasphematur inter gentes, id est a gentibus perfidis, quæ videntes vestram perversitatem, Deum vestrum blasphemant, æstimantes eum injustum qui tales servos asseritur elegisse, sicut scriptum est in Ezechiele, ubi prædicta verba habentur secundum translationem Septuaginta interpretum. Nostra autem translatio talis est : Ingressi sunt ad gentes, et polluerunt nomen meum. Et sicut Ezechiel ista dicebat de Judæis sibi contemporaneis, ad quos missus erat, sic Paulus hæc applicat Judæis sui temporis.
1.en: Further, what follows is to be understood as a question, with wonder and rebuke. [[2:21|Thou therefore, that teachest another, teachest not thyself|Qui ergo alium doces, te ipsum non doces?]] That is, since you presume to teach another, why do you not teach yourself? And it is strange that you do not teach yourself; and you do ill in not teaching yourself. In like manner are to be read the things that follow. [[2:21|thou, that preachest that men should not steal, stealest|Qui prædicas non furandum, furaris?]] [[2:22|Thou, that sayest men should not commit adultery, committest adultery|Qui dicis non mœchandum, mœcharis?]] And the Jews committed a spiritual theft and adultery as well, by withdrawing from the law its sense concerning Christ and its mystical understanding. [[2:22|thou, that abhorrest idols|Qui abominaris idola]], that is, the worship of idolatry, [[2:22|committest sacrilege|sacrilegium facis]], that is, theft and misuse of a sacred thing? For the Jews applied to their own uses some things set apart for divine worship, since the priests, Scribes and Pharisees were most covetous[[Luke 16:14||]]. For they made void the divine commandments by their superstitious traditions, as the Gospel says[[Matt 15:6||]]. [[2:23|Thou, that makest thy boast of the law|qui in lege gloriaris]], that is, of the receiving of the law, saying, [[Ps 77:3|How great things have we heard and known|Quanta audivimus et cognovimus ea]]; and, [[Ps 147:9|He hath not done in like manner to every nation|Non fecit taliter omni nationi]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlvii, 20, counting by the Hebrew]; [[2:23|by transgression of the law dishonourest God|per prævaricationem legis Deum inhonoras]], not showing him due reverence by obeying his commandments? [[2:24|For the name of God through you|Nomen enim Dei per vos]], that is, on your account, [[2:24|is blasphemed among the Gentiles|blasphematur inter gentes]], that is, by the faithless Gentiles, who, seeing your perversity, blaspheme your God, thinking him unjust who is declared to have chosen such servants, [[2:24|as it is written|sicut scriptum est]] in Ezechiel[[Ezech 36:20||]], where the words given above are found according to the translation of the Septuagint. But our translation reads thus: [[Ezech 36:20|when they entered among the nations whither they went, they profaned my holy name|Ingressi sunt ad gentes, et polluerunt nomen meum]]. And as Ezechiel said these things of the Jews of his own time, to whom he was sent, so Paul applies them to the Jews of his time.

1.t: Subinde ostendit Apostolus gravitatem excessus Judæorum ex conditione circumcisionis. Circumcisio namque erat signum justitiæ, et quædam professio legis servandæ, juxta illud Apostoli ad Galatas : Testificor omni homini circumcidenti se, quod debitor sit universæ legis faciendæ. Quemadmodum ergo nunc prodest professio vitæ claustralis, si regula observetur ; si vero regula omittatur, plurimum obest, et peccatum gravatur : sic de circumcisione erat tempore veteris Testamenti. Hoc est quod Apostolus subjungit.
1.en: Next the Apostle shows the gravity of the Jews' excess from the condition of circumcision. For circumcision was a sign of justice, and a kind of profession that the law would be kept, according to that of the Apostle to the Galatians: [[Gal 5:3|I testify again to every man circumcising himself that he is a debtor to do the whole law|Testificor omni homini circumcidenti se, quod debitor sit universæ legis faciendæ]]. As, then, the profession of the cloistered life profits now if the rule is kept, but if the rule is neglected it does very great harm and the sin is made heavier: so it was with circumcision in the time of the Old Testament. This is what the Apostle adds.

1.t: Circumcisio quidem prodest ad gratiam promerendam, videlicet tempore veteris Testamenti, non autem Evangelio divulgato, si legem observes. Si autem prævaricator legis Mosaicæ sis, circumcisio tua carnalis præputium facta est, id est præputio similis, non plus valens quam illud. Si ergo præputium, id est gentilis incircumcisus, justitias legis, id est præcepta moralia, quæ sunt de dictamine rationis naturalis, custodiat cum fide et cultu unius Dei, ut tactum est, nonne præputium illius in circumcisionem reputabitur, id est, tantum sibi proficiet ad salutem, ut tibi, o Judæe, circumcisio tua? quasi dicat, Ita. Custodiendo enim justitias legis modo præfato, spiritualiter circumciditur, et filius Abrahæ reputatur. Et judicabit id quod ex natura est præputium, id est gentilis præputium naturaliter habens, ex gentilibus ortus et in præputio natus, legem consummans, hoc est, justitias legis scriptæ adimplens ex naturali dictamine rationis : judicabit, inquam, id est, sui comparatione judicio damnationis dignum ostendet, […] Judæe. qui per litteram, id est legis scripturam, et circumcisionem prævaricator legis es, id est, nec per Scripturam sacram, neque per circumcisionis significationem a peccato retraheris, a quo gentilis retrahitur per legem naturalem sine circumcisione ac littera Scripturarum?
1.en: [[2:25|Circumcision profiteth indeed|Circumcisio quidem prodest]] for meriting grace, namely in the time of the Old Testament, but not once the Gospel has been published, [[2:25|if thou keep the law|si legem observes]]. [[2:25|but if thou be a transgressor of the law|Si autem prævaricator legis Mosaicæ sis]] of Moses, [[2:25|thy circumcision is made uncircumcision|circumcisio tua carnalis præputium facta est]] in the flesh, that is, like uncircumcision, worth no more than it. [[2:26|If then, the uncircumcised|Si ergo præputium]], that is, the uncircumcised Gentile, [[2:26|keep the justices of the law|justitias legis custodiat]], that is, the moral precepts, which are of the dictate of natural reason, with faith in and worship of the one God, as has been touched on, [[2:26|shall not this uncircumcision be counted for circumcision|nonne præputium illius in circumcisionem reputabitur]], that is, will it not profit him as much for salvation as your circumcision does you, O Jew? As if he were saying: So it is. For by keeping the justices of the law in the way mentioned he is spiritually circumcised, and is reckoned a son of Abraham. [[2:27|And shall not that which by nature is uncircumcision|Et judicabit id quod ex natura est præputium]], that is, the Gentile having uncircumcision by nature, born of Gentiles and in uncircumcision, [[2:27|if it fulfil the law|legem consummans]], that is, fulfilling the justices of the written law from the natural dictate of reason, [[2:27|judge thee|judicabit]], I say, that is, by comparison with himself show you worthy of the judgment of damnation, […] O Jew, [[2:27|who by the letter and circumcision art a transgressor of the law|qui per litteram et circumcisionem prævaricator legis es?]], that is, who are not drawn back from sin either by holy Scripture or by the meaning of circumcision, from which the Gentile is drawn back by the natural law without circumcision and the letter of the Scriptures?

1.t: Quod autem gentilis juste vivens, melior est Judæo circumciso injuste vivente, et eum condemnet, probat Apostolus, eo quod duplex sit circumcisio, scilicet spiritualis, et carnalis. Quarum prima facit spiritualem Judæum, secunda carnalem. Unde Propheta : Omnes, inquit, gentes habent præputium, omnis autem domus Israel incircumcisi sunt corde. Ad spiritualem vero circumcisionem admonet Moyses : Circumcidite, inquiens, præputium cordis vestri, et cervicem vestram ne induretis amplius. Et quantum caro est inferior spiritu, tantum circumcisio carnalis et carnalis Judæus inferiores sunt spirituali circumcisione atque Judæo. Ait itaque: Non enim qui in manifesto, id est, qui circumcisus est carne, et potest hominibus signum Judaismi ostendere, Judæus est solum et vere : Judæus enim interpretatur confitens, quod competit non solum circumciso ; neque quæ in manifesto, in carne, est circumcisio, id est, circumcisio illa exterior pelliculam tollens, est circumcisio perfecta ac vera. Sed qui in abscondito, id est, qui corde circumcisus est (quæ circumcisio homines latet, Deoque patet), Judæus est vere ac spiritualiter, confitens Domino confessione laudis divinæ : […] […] dis, id est circumcisio spiritualis facta in spiritu, id est secundum spiritualem intellectum Scripturæ veteris Testamenti, non littera, id est non secundum sensum litteralem ipsius ; vel, In spiritu, id est virtute Spiritus Sancti, non littera, id est litteralibus cultris legis. Cujus, videlicet spiritualis circumcisionis, laus non […] ex hominibus, qui in interiori loco non valent, neque de eis certum quidquam […] judicant, sed […] qui inspector […]
1.en: And that the Gentile who lives justly is better than the circumcised Jew who lives unjustly, and condemns him, the Apostle proves from this, that circumcision is twofold, namely spiritual and carnal. The first of these makes the spiritual Jew, the second the carnal. Hence the Prophet says: [[Jer 9:26|all the nations are uncircumcised in the flesh, but all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in the heart|Omnes, inquit, gentes habent præputium, omnis autem domus Israel incircumcisi sunt corde]] [Denis has "all nations have the foreskin"]. And Moses admonishes to spiritual circumcision: [[Deut 10:16|Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and stiffen your neck no more|Circumcidite, inquiens, præputium cordis vestri, et cervicem vestram ne induretis amplius]] (he says). And as much as the flesh is lower than the spirit, so much are carnal circumcision and the carnal Jew lower than the spiritual circumcision and the spiritual Jew. He says, therefore: [[2:28|For it is not he is a Jew, who is so outwardly|Non enim qui in manifesto, Judæus est]], that is, he who is circumcised in the flesh and can show men the sign of Judaism is not only and truly a Jew: for *Jew* means one who confesses [praises], which belongs not only to the circumcised; [[2:28|nor is that circumcision which is outwardly in the flesh|neque quæ in manifesto, in carne, est circumcisio]], that is, that outward circumcision which removes a little skin is not perfect and true circumcision. [[2:29|But he is a Jew that is one inwardly|sed qui in abscondito, Judæus est]], that is, he who is circumcised in heart (which circumcision is hidden from men and open to God) is truly and spiritually a Jew, confessing the Lord with the confession of divine praise: […] [[2:29|and the circumcision is that of the heart|circumcisio]] [the transcription is unreadable here], that is, the spiritual circumcision made [[2:29|in the spirit|in spiritu]], that is, according to the spiritual understanding of the Scripture of the Old Testament, [[2:29|not in the letter|non littera]], that is, not according to its literal sense; or, *in the spirit*, that is, by the power of the Holy Ghost, *not in the letter*, that is, by the literal knives of the law. [[2:29|whose praise is not of men|Cujus … laus non … ex hominibus]], namely of the spiritual circumcision, who cannot reach the inward place, nor […] judge anything certain about them, but […] who, the searcher [… the rest of this sentence is unreadable in the transcription].

3.title: Elucidatio capi[tis tertii] […]
3.note: The beginning of this article (the title and the commentary on verses 1–4) and parts of the commentary on verses 19–20, 25 and 26 are missing from the transcription; they await a scan of the page.

paras.t: […] nem, qua mihi pollicitus es quod ex semine meo humanam naturam assumeres: ex quo constat te verum esse in promissis; et vincas, id est, prævaleas aliis, quum judicaris ab eis non debere promissionem tuam mihi de Christo factam implere propter scelera mea. Quum enim David uxorem Uriæ violasset et cognovisset, ejusque virum occidisset, multi dicebant prædictam promissionem evacuatam, quoniam non deceret Christum de homicida et adultero nasci. Quum ergo Deus hujus dicti oppositum fecit, prævaluit istis. Hunc sensum intendit hoc loco Apostolus. Possunt quoque prædicta verba adhuc tribus modis exponi, sicut in expositione libri Psalmorum induxi; sed hoc loco iste sufficiat. Sciendum vero quod hæc dictio, Ut, secundum hunc sensum, tenetur consecutive, non autem causaliter: quia non ideo David peccavit, ut Deus justificaretur, sed ex ejus peccato occasionaliter consecuta est manifestatio divinæ justitiæ, juxta modum expositum.
paras.en: […] [the opening of this article, on Romans 3:1–4, is missing from the transcription; the text resumes in the middle of the gloss on *in thy words*] the promise by which you promised me that you would take human nature from my seed: from which it is clear that you are true in your promises; [[3:4|and mayest overcome|et vincas]], that is, prevail over others, [[3:4|when thou art judged|quum judicaris]] by them not bound to fulfil the promise you made me of Christ, because of my crimes. For when David had violated and known the wife of Urias[[2 Kings 11:4||]] and had killed her husband[[2 Kings 11:15||]][[2 Kings 11:17||]], many said that the promise just mentioned had been made void, since it would not be fitting for Christ to be born of a murderer and an adulterer. So when God did the opposite of what they said, he prevailed over them. This is the sense the Apostle intends in this place. The words can also be explained in three further ways, as I set out in the exposition of the book of Psalms; but here let this one suffice. It must be known, however, that the word *that*, in this sense, is taken consecutively and not causally: for David did not sin in order that God might be justified, but from his sin there followed, as an occasion, the showing forth of the divine justice, in the way explained.

paras.t: Sed quoniam ex prædictis verbis David, quibus ait, Malum coram te feci ut justificeris, etc., quidam sumpserunt occasionem erroris, dicentes, quod nostra peccata atque mendacia directe faciunt ad gloriam Dei, videlicet ad manifestationem divinæ veritatis atque justitiæ, et per consequens, quod Deus vellet nos peccare et mentiri, quatenus comparatione nostri justior ac verior, imo solus justus ac verus appareret, et ut misericors agnosceretur dum nobis ignosceret: hoc sanctus Apostolus reprobat, ducendo ad inconveniens. Ait ergo: Si autem iniquitas nostra justitiam Dei commendat, id est, directe et per se commendabilem seu laudabilem facit, ut aliqui asserunt, quid dicemus? id est, quid respondere poterimus ad ea quæ sequuntur ex hoc? Primo enim sequeretur Deum esse injustum, qui peccatum ulciscitur. Ideo subdit: Numquid iniquus est Deus qui infert iram, id est pœnam pro culpa?
paras.en: But since from these words of David, in which he says, [[Ps 50:6|have done evil before thee: that thou mayst be justified|Malum coram te feci ut justificeris]], etc., some took occasion for error, saying that our sins and lies work directly for the glory of God, namely for the showing forth of the divine truth and justice, and consequently that God would have us sin and lie, so that by comparison with us he might appear more just and more true, nay, alone just and true, and might be known as merciful in pardoning us: this the holy Apostle refutes by leading it to an absurdity. So he says: [[3:5|But if our injustice commend the justice of God|Si autem iniquitas nostra justitiam Dei commendat]], that is, makes it directly and of itself commendable or praiseworthy, as some assert, [[3:5|what shall we say?|quid dicemus?]] that is, what shall we be able to answer to what follows from this? For first it would follow that God, who punishes sin, is unjust. Therefore he adds: [[3:5|Is God unjust, who executeth wrath?|Numquid iniquus est Deus qui infert iram]], that is, punishment for guilt?

paras.t: Secundum hominem dico. Absit: hoc est, sic ego esse non assero, sed secundum carnales hoc sequitur. Quod enim per se facit ad gloriam Dei, non est puniendum, sed præmiandum ut bonum, quia per se ordinatur ad finem laudabilem. Si ergo iniquitas nostra per se facit ad gloriam Dei, injustus est Deus qui vindicat eam per tormenta. Alioqui, quomodo judicabit Deus hunc mundum, id est homines peregrinantes in terra? Si enim injustus est Deus, non poterit mundum hunc juste judicare, quia justitia maxime spectat ad judicem, prout Sapiens dicit: Diligite justitiam, qui judicatis terram. Quod autem non sit Deus injustus, elucescit ex verbo Psalmistæ dicentis: Quoniam rectus Dominus Deus noster, et non est iniquitas in eo. Unde Josaphat aiebat: Non est apud Dominum Deum nostrum iniquitas, nec personarum acceptio, neque acceptio munerum. Deus quippe gloriosus et fortis est ipsa essentia bonitatis, mensura et causa totius æquitatis: ideo culpa ei placere non potest. Quod confirmat Apostolus, subdens:
paras.en: [[3:6|I speak according to man. God forbid!|Secundum hominem dico. Absit]]: that is, I do not assert that it is so, but according to carnal men this follows. For what of itself works for the glory of God is not to be punished but rewarded as good, since of itself it is ordered to a praiseworthy end. If, then, our iniquity of itself works for the glory of God, God is unjust in avenging it by torments. [[3:6|Otherwise how shall God judge this world?|Alioqui, quomodo judicabit Deus hunc mundum]], that is, men who are pilgrims on earth? For if God is unjust, he will not be able to judge this world justly, since justice belongs above all to a judge, as the Wise man says: [[Wis 1:1|Love justice, you that are the judges of the earth|Diligite justitiam, qui judicatis terram]]. That God is not unjust shines out from the word of the Psalmist, who says: [[Ps 91:16|That the Lord our God is righteous, and there is no iniquity in him|Quoniam rectus Dominus Deus noster, et non est iniquitas in eo]]. Hence Josaphat said: [[2 Par 19:7|there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor desire of gifts|Non est apud Dominum Deum nostrum iniquitas, nec personarum acceptio, neque acceptio munerum]]. For God, glorious and strong, is the very essence of goodness, the measure and cause of all equity: therefore guilt cannot please him. This the Apostle confirms, adding:

paras.t: Si enim veritas, id est æquitas, Dei in meo mendacio, id est per meum peccatum, abundavit, id est, quantum ad sui manifestationem directe crevit, clariusque innotuit: et hoc, in gloriam ipsius Dei, ita quod ex meo peccato per se gloriosior perfectiorque apparet; quid adhuc et ego tanquam peccator judicor? id est, cur nunc usque injustus existimor? tanquam dicat: Si sic esset, non essem reputandus iniquus, quia non displiceret Deo iniquitas mea, ut dictum est.
paras.en: [[3:7|For if the truth of God|Si enim veritas Dei]], that is, his equity, [[3:7|through my lie|in meo mendacio]], that is, through my sin, [[3:7|hath more abounded|abundavit]], that is, has directly grown as to its being shown forth, and become more clearly known: and this [[3:7|unto his glory|in gloriam ipsius]], God's, so that from my sin he of himself appears more glorious and more perfect; [[3:7|why am I also yet judged as a sinner?|quid adhuc et ego tanquam peccator judicor?]] that is, why am I still held to be unjust? As if he said: if it were so, I should not be reckoned wicked, since my iniquity would not displease God, as has been said.

paras.t: Deinde destruit præmemoratum errorem, ducendo ad aliud inconveniens. Et non sicut blasphemamur, hoc est, si nostra peccata directe ordinantur ac operantur ad glorificationem divinæ justitiæ, sicut illi dixerunt, cur ita non est sicut nobis blasphemiæ imponitur? et sicut aiunt quidam nos dicere, id est, sicut pseudoapostoli affirmant me aliosque veros Apostolos prædicare illud quod sequitur, faciamus mala ut veniant bona? quorum pseudoapostolorum, qui nobis ista imponunt, damnatio justa est, quia mortaliter peccant. Quoniam enim Apostolus ait inferius, Ubi abundavit delictum, abundavit et gratia; et nunc simile aliquid dixit, allegando verba Psalmistæ; alii quoque Apostoli talia prædicaverunt: ex his moti sunt æmuli Apostolorum, dicentes quod prædicarent peccata esse patranda et continuanda, quatenus ex hoc sequerentur bona, videlicet glorificatio seu manifestatio divinæ æquitatis ac pietatis.
paras.en: Then he overthrows the error mentioned by leading it to another absurdity. [[3:8|And not rather (as we are slandered|Et non sicut blasphemamur]], that is, if our sins are directly ordered and work for the glorifying of the divine justice, as they said, why is it not so as the slander laid upon us has it? [[3:8|and as some affirm that we say)|et sicut aiunt quidam nos dicere]], that is, as the false apostles assert that I and the other true Apostles preach what follows: [[3:8|let us do evil that there may come good?|faciamus mala ut veniant bona?]] [[3:8|Whose damnation is just|quorum damnatio justa est]], that of the false apostles who lay these things upon us, for they sin mortally. For since the Apostle says further on, [[Rom 5:20|where sin abounded, grace did more abound|Ubi abundavit delictum, abundavit et gratia]] [Denis: "grace abounded too"], and now said something similar by alleging the words of the Psalmist, and the other Apostles too preached such things, the rivals of the Apostles were moved by these to say that they preached that sins were to be committed and kept up, so that good might follow from it, namely the glorifying or showing forth of the divine equity and mercy.

paras.t: Præterea advertendum, quod quum peccatum sit aversio mentis a Deo, et recessus ab ordine, secundum Dionysium, et ab eo quod est secundum naturam, secundum Damascenum; idcirco per peccatum irrogatur Deo injuria, et directe inhonoratur Deus, non glorificatur. Verumtamen, quoniam tanta est bonitas Dei, ut non permitteret malum, nisi prænosceret aliud bonum inde venturum; et tanta est virtus ejus, quod malum omnino impediret, nisi aliquod bonum ex malo elicere posset: propterea malum culpæ indirecte atque per accidens, scilicet præter propriam conditionem, et præter peccantis intentionem, ordinatur et valet ad declarationem divinæ justitiæ, secundum quod Deus per pœnam ordinat culpam. In quo divina sapientia atque justitia manifeste refulget: quemadmodum etiam ex crudelitate tyrannorum, præter intentionem ipsorum, manifestavit Deus patientiam atque constantiam martyrum.
paras.en: It must be noted further that since sin is a turning away of the mind from God and a departing from order, according to Dionysius, and from what is according to nature, according to Damascene, therefore by sin injury is done to God, and God is directly dishonoured, not glorified. Yet since the goodness of God is so great that he would not permit evil unless he foreknew that some other good would come of it, and his power so great that he would wholly prevent evil unless he could draw some good out of it, therefore the evil of guilt, indirectly and by accident, that is, apart from its own character and apart from the sinner's intention, is ordered to and serves the showing forth of the divine justice, inasmuch as God orders guilt by punishment. In which the divine wisdom and justice plainly shine out: as also from the cruelty of tyrants, apart from their intention, God has shown forth the patience and constancy of the martyrs.

paras.t: Jam declaravit Apostolus, Judæos excellentiores fuisse gentilibus pro tempore legis scriptæ; nunc sciscitatur, an etiam tempore evangelicæ legis Judæi excellant gentiles. Quid ergo restat? Præcellimus nos Judæi eos, id est gentiles ad fidem conversos? Nequaquam. Loquitur autem Apostolus de utroque populo isto in genere. Certum est enim, quod in speciali loquendo, ipsi beati Apostoli, qui erant Judæi, et primitias Spiritus receperunt, ceteris eminebant. Loquendo vero in generali, omnes pares sunt in gratia Evangelii, sicut clarius ostendetur. Cur autem non excellant Judæi gentiles, annectitur. Causati enim sumus, id est, rationabiliter declaravimus, Judæos et Græcos, id est gentiles, omnes sub peccato esse, quia Judæi transgressi sunt legem scriptam, gentiles legem naturalem.
paras.en: The Apostle has already made plain that the Jews were more excellent than the Gentiles during the time of the written law; now he asks whether in the time of the law of the Gospel too the Jews excel the Gentiles. [[3:9|What then?|Quid ergo]] remains? [[3:9|Do we excel them?|Præcellimus eos?]] we Jews, them, that is, the Gentiles converted to the faith? [[3:9|No, not so|Nequaquam]]. The Apostle is speaking of each of these peoples in general. For it is certain that, speaking in particular, the blessed Apostles themselves, who were Jews and received [[Rom 8:23|the firstfruits of the Spirit|primitias Spiritus]], stood out above the rest. But speaking in general, all are equal in the grace of the Gospel, as will be shown more clearly. Why the Jews do not excel the Gentiles is added: [[3:9|For we have charged|Causati enim sumus]], that is, we have shown by reasoning, [[3:9|both Jews and Greeks|Judæos et Græcos]], that is, Gentiles, [[3:9|that they are all under sin|omnes sub peccato esse]], since the Jews transgressed the written law, the Gentiles the natural law.

paras.t: Sicut scriptum est in Psalmo, quantum ad sensum: Quia non est justus quisquam, justitia meritoria, propriis viribus; non est intelligens ea quæ Dei sunt, per fidem formatam, sine lumine gratiæ, non est requirens Deum per opera sancta, propria potestate. Omnes isti jam dicti declinaverunt a Deo atque justitia, simul inutiles, id est vani, facti sunt, non pertingendo ad ultimum finem, seu veram felicitatem; non est qui faciat per se, sine auxilio gratiæ, bonum, id est opus meritorium, non est usque ad unum, id est, omnino nullus est. Vel, Non est usque ad unum, id est, non est alius præter Christum Deum et hominem, qui sub peccato non fuit, et ea quæ placuerunt Patri, semper effecit.
paras.en: [[3:10|As it is written|sicut scriptum est]] in the Psalm[[Ps 13:1||]], as to the sense: [[3:10|There is not any man just|Quia non est justus quisquam]], with meritorious justice, by his own strength; [[3:11|There is none that understandeth|non est intelligens]] the things that are of God, by formed faith, without the light of grace; [[3:11|there is none that seeketh after God|non est requirens Deum]] by holy works, by his own power. [[3:12|All have turned out of the way|Omnes declinaverunt]], all those just spoken of, from God and from justice; [[3:12|they are become unprofitable together|simul inutiles facti sunt]], that is, vain, not reaching their last end, or true happiness; [[3:12|there is none that doth good|non est qui faciat bonum]] of himself, without the help of grace, good, that is, a meritorious work; [[3:12|there is not so much as one|non est usque ad unum]], that is, there is none at all. Or, *there is not so much as one*, that is, there is no other besides Christ, God and man, who was not under sin and [[John 8:29|do always the things that please him|ea quæ placuerunt Patri, semper effecit]] [Denis: "always did the things that pleased the Father"].

paras.t: Sepulcrum patens est guttur eorum, id est simile monumento aperto, quoniam sicut ex tali sepulcro ascendit fœtor cadaveris, sic ex ore istorum procedunt verba mortua atque fœtentia; linguis suis dolose agebant, alios decipiendo, vel sophistica et adulatoria verba loquendo. Unde ait Scriptura: Qui sophistice loquitur, odibilis est; in omni re defraudabitur. Non est illi data a Deo gratia: omni enim sapientia defraudatus est. Quocontra de electis Judæis scriptum est: Reliquiæ Israel non facient iniquitatem, nec loquentur mendacium; et non invenietur in ore eorum lingua dolosa. Venenum aspidum, id est verba venenata ac detractoria, seu odium insanabile, sub labiis eorum, quia parati sunt talia verba evomere, aliosque inficere. Quorum os maledictione, hoc est verbis maledicis ac blasphemis, et amaritudine, id est sermonibus pungitivis, plenum est.
paras.en: [[3:13|Their throat is an open sepulchre|Sepulcrum patens est guttur eorum]], that is, like an open tomb, since as the stench of a corpse rises from such a sepulchre, so from the mouth of these come dead and stinking words; [[3:13|with their tongues they have dealt deceitfully|linguis suis dolose agebant]], deceiving others, or speaking sophistical and flattering words. Hence the Scripture says: [[Ecclus 37:23|He that speaketh sophistically, is hateful: he shall be destitute of every thing|Qui sophistice loquitur, odibilis est; in omni re defraudabitur]]. [[Ecclus 37:24|Grace is not given him from the Lord: for he is deprived of all wisdom|Non est illi data a Deo gratia: omni enim sapientia defraudatus est]]. Whereas of the chosen Jews it is written: [[Soph 3:13|The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies, nor shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth|Reliquiæ Israel non facient iniquitatem, nec loquentur mendacium; et non invenietur in ore eorum lingua dolosa]]. [[3:13|The venom of asps|Venenum aspidum]], that is, poisoned and slanderous words, or incurable hatred, [[3:13|is under their lips|sub labiis eorum]], for they are ready to spew out such words and infect others. [[3:14|Whose mouth is full of cursing|quorum os maledictione, et amaritudine plenum est]], that is, of cursing and blasphemous words, [[3:14|and bitterness|et amaritudine]], that is, of stinging speech.

paras.t: Veloces pedes eorum spirituales, puta affectus, et etiam corporales, ut currant ad effundendum sanguinem innocentem. Contritio, hoc est spiritualis destructio, temporalis punitio, seu omnis boni dissipatio, et infelicitas, id est miseria, in viis, id est operibus eorum. Committendo enim mala prædicta, amittunt esse gratuitum, spirituale ac meritorium, et tanquam inane ac nihilum reputantur a Deo, et miseri sunt, tanquam æterna damnatione condigni. Et viam pacis, id est opera bona, per quæ ad veram pacem pertingitur; vel, Viam pacis, id est pacem hujus viæ et gratiæ perducentem ad plenam pacem patriæ; non cognoverunt per approbationem ac imitationem. Non est timor Dei ante oculos eorum, id est, Deum non metuunt, nec oculis cordis sui divinum proponunt timorem, sed inanissima securitate resolvuntur.
paras.en: [[3:15|Their feet swift|Veloces pedes eorum]], their spiritual feet, namely the affections, and their bodily ones too, so that they run [[3:15|to shed blood|ad effundendum sanguinem]], innocent blood. [[3:16|Destruction|Contritio]], that is, spiritual ruin, temporal punishment, or the scattering of all good, [[3:16|and misery|et infelicitas]], that is, wretchedness, [[3:16|in their ways|in viis eorum]], that is, their works. For by committing the evils mentioned they lose the being of grace, spiritual and meritorious, and are reckoned by God as empty and nothing[[Is 40:17||]], and are wretched, as men deserving eternal damnation. [[3:17|And the way of peace|Et viam pacis]], that is, good works, by which true peace is reached; or, *the way of peace*, that is, the peace of this way and of grace that leads to the full peace of the fatherland; [[3:17|they have not known|non cognoverunt]] by approving and imitating it. [[3:18|There is no fear of God before their eyes|Non est timor Dei ante oculos eorum]], that is, they do not fear God, nor set the divine fear before the eyes of their heart, but are slackened in a most empty security.

paras.t: Multi arbitrantur Apostolum, allegatam scripturam sumpsisse ex psalmo in quo prædicta verba conscripta sunt; sed secundum Hieronymum ita non est. Advertendum ergo, quod quum Hieronymus in prologo quintidecimi libri sui super Isaiam dixisset, Christum et Evangelistas atque Apostolos ea dumtaxat verba Scripturæ ex translatione Septuaginta interpretum allegare, quæ cum Hebraica veritate concordant, virgo Christi Eustochium, femina religiosa atque doctissima, objecit Hieronymo, quod Apostolus ad Romanos octo versus allegarit ex psalmo tertiodecimo, qui in Hebræo non habentur, videlicet, Sepulcrum patens est guttur eorum, usque ad id inclusive, Non est timor Dei ante oculos, etc., et videtur Apostolus ex translatione Septuaginta interpretum allegasse, vel ex psalmo illo, quod in Hebræo non habetur. Ad hanc objectionem stupefactus, pallidusque effectus Hieronymus, prout ipse testatur, quasi a fortissimo pugile cæsus, unius diei spatio postulato, et perlustrata Scriptura respondit, quod tota pene epistola ad Romanos de veteri Testamento constructa est. Præmemoratum quoque testimonium octo versuum ex Psalmis et Isaia contextum est. Nam duo primi versus, videlicet, Sepulcrum patens est guttur eorum, Linguis suis dolose agebant, in quinto psalmo habentur. Quod autem subjungitur, Venenum aspidum sub labiis eorum, in psalmo centesimo tricesimo nono legitur, qui incipit, Eripe me, Domine, ab homine malo. Porro quod subditur, Quorum os maledictione et amaritudine plenum est, ex nono sumptum est psalmo. Alii vero tres versus, Veloces pedes eorum ad effundendum sanguinem, etc., ex quinquagesimo nono capitulo Isaiæ accepti noscuntur, ubi sic legitur: Pedes eorum ad malum currunt, et festinant ut effundant sanguinem innocentem; vastitas et contritio in viis eorum, et viam pacis nescierunt. Ultimus vero versiculus, scilicet, Non est timor Dei ante oculos eorum, in principio psalmi tricesimi quinti habetur, quo dicitur, Dixit injustus ut delinquat in semetipso, non est timor Dei ante oculos ejus: Apostolus tamen allegat pluraliter, quia pluribus loquebatur.
paras.en: Many think that the Apostle took the scripture he alleges from the psalm in which these words are written; but according to Jerome it is not so. It must be noted, then, that when Jerome, in the prologue to the fifteenth book of his commentary on Isaias, had said that Christ and the Evangelists and Apostles allege from the translation of the Seventy only those words of Scripture which agree with the Hebrew truth, the virgin of Christ Eustochium, a religious and most learned woman, objected to Jerome that the Apostle, in the Epistle to the Romans, alleges eight verses from the thirteenth psalm which are not found in the Hebrew, namely from [[Ps 13:3|Their throat is an open sepulchre|Sepulcrum patens est guttur eorum]] up to and including [[Ps 13:3|there is no fear of God before their eyes|Non est timor Dei ante oculos]], etc.; and the Apostle seems to have alleged them from the translation of the Seventy, or from that psalm, which is not found so in the Hebrew. At this objection Jerome was astounded and turned pale, as he himself testifies, as though struck by a very strong boxer; and having asked for the space of one day, and searched through the Scripture, he answered that almost the whole Epistle to the Romans is built from the Old Testament. The testimony of eight verses just mentioned is also woven together from the Psalms and Isaias. For the first two verses, namely, [[Ps 5:11|Their throat is an open sepulchre: they dealt deceitfully with their tongues|Sepulcrum patens est guttur eorum, Linguis suis dolose agebant]], are found in the fifth psalm. What follows, [[Ps 139:4|the venom of asps is under their lips|Venenum aspidum sub labiis eorum]], is read in the hundred and thirty-ninth psalm, which begins, [[Ps 139:2|Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man|Eripe me, Domine, ab homine malo]]. Further, what is added, [[Ps 9:28|His mouth is full of cursing, and of bitterness|Quorum os maledictione et amaritudine plenum est]] [Denis: "whose mouth"], is taken from the ninth psalm. The other three verses, [[3:15|Their feet swift to shed blood|Veloces pedes eorum ad effundendum sanguinem]], etc., are known to be taken from the fifty-ninth chapter of Isaias, where we read thus: [[Is 59:7|Their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed innocent blood|Pedes eorum ad malum currunt, et festinant ut effundant sanguinem innocentem]]; [[Is 59:7|wasting and destruction are in their ways|vastitas et contritio in viis eorum]], [[Is 59:8|They have not known the way of peace|et viam pacis nescierunt]]. The last verse, namely, [[3:18|There is no fear of God before their eyes|Non est timor Dei ante oculos eorum]], is found at the beginning of the thirty-fifth psalm, where it is said: [[Ps 35:2|The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin: there is no fear of God before his eyes|Dixit injustus ut delinquat in semetipso, non est timor Dei ante oculos ejus]]. The Apostle, however, alleges it in the plural, because he was speaking to many.

paras.t: Itaque prædicti versus nec in Hebræo, nec in Septuaginta interpretibus habentur, quantum ad psalmum tertiumdecimum, sed in editione vulgata. Lyra tamen asserit prædicta ex psalmo tertiodecimo allegata. Sed consentiendum est verbis Hieronymi: qui etiam ait, quod Græci expositores exponendo psalmum tertiumdecimum prædictos versus veru prænotant, neque exponunt.
paras.en: So the verses mentioned are found, as regards the thirteenth psalm, neither in the Hebrew nor in the Seventy, but in the common edition. Lyra, however, asserts that they are alleged from the thirteenth psalm. But we must agree with the words of Jerome, who also says that the Greek expositors, in expounding the thirteenth psalm, mark these verses beforehand with an obelus [*veru*, the critical sign for a spurious passage] and do not expound them.

paras.t: Sciendum autem quod Apostolus loquitur, his qui in lege sunt loquitur. Ex hoc multi affirmant, præinductam scripturam ad Judæorum populum pertinere, qui soli sub lege Moysis erant, de qua nunc tractat Apostolus. Sed obviat, quod Apostolus istam scripturam inducit ad ostendendum quod Judæi et Græci omnes sub peccato fuerunt, et quod nunc protinus subditur, ut om […] tur, et subditus fiat omnis […] Est igitur sensus: Scim […] Apostoli, Spiritu Sancto ed […] Scripturas ceteris clarius […] Testamenti Scriptura, loqu […] in lege Moysis sunt loque […] principaliter, quemadmodu […] tor: Non sum missus nisi […] perierunt domus Israel. E […] stolus retundendo Judæoru […] scilicet, ne dicerent scriptu […] non pertinere ad eos, se […] dumtaxat. Itaque lex dicit […] Judæis, ut omne os præsu […] struatur, id est, ut nec […] Judæus præsumat se inanit […] justificare, eo quod, testa […] omnes peccato obnoxii sin […] fiat omnis mundus, id est […] Judæus et Græcus, Deo, cog […] priam vilitatem et culpam […] quoque ad divinam pietate […] quasi non potens aliter sa […]
paras.en: [[3:19|Now we know that what things soever the law speaketh, it speaketh to them that are in the law|Scimus autem quoniam quæcumque lex loquitur, his qui in lege sunt loquitur]] [the transcription garbles the first words of this lemma]. From this many affirm that the scripture alleged above concerns the people of the Jews, who alone were under the law of Moses, of which the Apostle is now treating. But against this is the fact that the Apostle brings in this scripture to show that Jews and Greeks were all under sin, and what is added straight after, [[3:19|that every mouth may be stopped and all the world may be made subject to God|ut omne os obstruatur, et subditus fiat omnis mundus Deo]]. The sense, then, is: we know […] Apostles, taught by the Holy Ghost […] the Scriptures more clearly than others […] the Scripture of the […] Testament speaks […] to those who are in the law of Moses […] chiefly, as the Saviour […]: *I was not sent but to the sheep that are lost of the house of Israel*[[Matt 15:24||]] […] the Apostle, beating back the Jews […], namely, lest they should say that the scripture did not concern them, but […] only. So the law says […] to the Jews, *that every mouth* of the presumptuous *may be stopped*, that is, that neither […] nor Jew may presume to justify himself vainly […], since, as [Scripture] testifies, all are liable to sin; [[3:19|and all the world may be made subject|et subditus fiat omnis mundus]], that is, […] Jew and Greek, [[3:19|to God|Deo]], acknowledging […] his own vileness and guilt […] also to the divine mercy […] as one unable to be saved otherwise […] [in this part of the page the transcription has kept only half of each line of the left column].

paras.t: Præterea lex vetus tribu […] pitur: Primo communite […] toto Testamento antiquo: s […] omnes libros canonicos vet […] ti. Et ita sumitur, dum ait […] impleatur sermo qui in leg […] ptus est, Quia odio habue […] tis. Hoc enim habetur in […] liter quum Christus ait Ju […] vestra scriptum est: Ego […] Secundo accipitur proprie […] cho seu quinque libris Mo […] dicitur: Oportet impleri o […] pta sunt in lege, et Prophe […] de me. Tertio sumitur stric […] ptis cærimonialibus, ut qu […] Quia ex operibus legis, id […] vatione cærimoniarum præ […] videlicet sacrificiorum, cir […] solennitatum custodia, non […] rum et vitulorum auferri peccata, aut gratiam adipisci. Non enim gratiam conferebant, nec meritoria erant ex se, seu opere operato, sed ex fide et devotione observantium, id est ratione operis operantis. Opera vero præceptorum moralium justificabant, non tamen sine fide Christi et gratia Dei. Per legem enim scriptam, cognitio peccati, id est, ex ipsa lege cognoscitur quid sit malum; non autem vitatur virtute legis, sed per gratiam Dei. Hoc autem non est sic intelligendum, quasi ante legislationem nescierint homines quæ opera essent vitiosa, sed quia non ita perfecte cognoscebantur peccata secundum gradus et species suas.
paras.en: Further, the old law is taken in three [ways]: first, commonly, [for] the whole Old Testament, [that is, for] all the canonical books of the Old Testament. And it is taken so when [Christ] says: [*That*] *the word may be fulfilled which is written in their law: they hated me without cause*[[John 15:25||]]. For this is found in [the Psalm][[Ps 34:19||]]. [Likewise] when Christ says to the Jews: [*Is it not*] *written in your law: I said* [*you are gods*][[John 10:34||]]. Secondly, it is taken properly [for the Pentateuch], or the five books of Moses, [as when] it is said: *all things must needs be fulfilled which are written in the law* […] *and in the prophets* […] *concerning me*[[Luke 24:44||]]. Thirdly, it is taken strictly [for the] ceremonial [precepts], as [here]: [[3:20|Because by the works of the law|Quia ex operibus legis]], that is, [by the] observance of the ceremonies [commanded], namely of sacrifices, [circumcision], and the keeping of solemnities, [[3:20|no flesh shall be justified before him|non justificabitur omnis caro coram illo]] […] [for it was impossible that by the blood of goats] and calves sins should be taken away, or grace obtained. For they did not confer grace, nor were they meritorious of themselves, or *ex opere operato* [by the work done], but from the faith and devotion of those who observed them, that is, by reason of the work of the worker [*ex opere operantis*]. The works of the moral precepts did justify, yet not without faith in Christ and the grace of God. [[3:20|For by the law is the knowledge of sin|Per legem enim scriptam, cognitio peccati]], the written law, that is, from the law itself it is known what is evil; but it is not avoided by the power of the law, but through the grace of God. This is not to be understood as if before the giving of the law men did not know what works were vicious, but that sins were not so perfectly known according to their degrees and kinds.

paras.t: Deinde ostendit hominem justificari sine operibus legis, ex perfectione fidei christianæ. Nunc autem, id est tempore gratiæ atque evangelicæ legis, justitia Dei, id est justificatio quam Deus clementer et gratiose efficit in nobis, peccata tollendo et gratiam infundendo, sine lege, id est Mosaicæ legis observatione, manifestata est in gentibus ad fidem conversis per diversa miracula, quibus Deus declaravit fidem eorum sibi esse acceptam, quamvis non observaverint legem: quemadmodum in Actibus legitur, quod Deus in signo visibili dedit Spiritum Sanctum Cornelio centurioni gentili, et his qui erant cum eo. Justitia, inquam, testificata, id est prænuntiata ac testimonium habens, a lege, id est ex libris Moysis, in quibus multa de Christo et ejus justificatione quam facit in nobis, prædicuntur verbis et signis, et Prophetis, qui de eadem re manifestius vaticinati sunt, et de futura in nobis gratia prædixerunt, secundum principem Apostolorum. De missione enim Spiritus Sancti Deus per Joelem prædixit: Effundam de Spiritu meo super omnem carnem. Propter quod Petrus de Christo loquens: Huic, inquit, omnes Prophetæ testimo […]
paras.en: Then he shows that man is justified without the works of the law, from the perfection of the Christian faith. [[3:21|But now|Nunc autem]], that is, in the time of grace and of the law of the Gospel, [[3:21|the justice of God|justitia Dei]], that is, the justification which God works in us mercifully and graciously, taking away sins and pouring in grace, [[3:21|without the law|sine lege]], that is, without the observance of the law of Moses, [[3:21|is made manifest|manifestata est]] in the Gentiles converted to the faith, through various miracles, by which God declared that their faith was acceptable to him, though they did not observe the law: as we read in the Acts that God, by a visible sign, gave the Holy Ghost to Cornelius, a Gentile centurion, and to those who were with him[[Acts 10:44||]]. The justice, I say, [[3:21|being witnessed|testificata]], that is, foretold and having testimony, [[3:21|by the law|a lege]], that is, from the books of Moses, in which many things about Christ and the justification he works in us are foretold in words and signs, [[3:21|and the prophets|et Prophetis]], who prophesied of the same thing more plainly, and foretold the grace to come in us[[1 Pet 1:10||]], according to the prince of the Apostles. For of the sending of the Holy Ghost God foretold through Joel: [[Joel 2:28|I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh|Effundam de Spiritu meo super omnem carnem]]. For which reason Peter, speaking of Christ, says: [[Acts 10:43|To him all the prophets give testimony|Huic omnes Prophetæ testimonium perhibent]] […] [the rest of this sentence is missing from the transcription].

paras.t: Justitia autem Dei, id est nobis a Deo collata est, per fidem formatam Jesu Christi, id est per fidem catholicam, cujus objectum et causa est Christus. Fides enim est fundamentum justitiæ. Unde Christus frequenter in Evangelio loquitur: Fides tua te salvum fecit. In omnes Judæos, et super omnes gentiles, qui credunt in eum, hoc est in Christum per fidem formatam, secundum quod in Actibus dicitur: In hoc omnis qui credit, justificatur; et rursus: Deus fide purificans corda eorum. Non enim est distinctio Judæi et Græci tempore evangelicæ legis, quantum ad justificationem prædictam, quia non est personarum acceptor Deus. Et sicut Salvator aiebat: Qui crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit.
paras.en: [[3:22|Even the justice of God|Justitia autem Dei]], that is, bestowed on us by God, is [[3:22|by faith of Jesus Christ|per fidem formatam Jesu Christi]], formed faith, that is, by the Catholic faith, whose object and cause is Christ. For faith is the foundation of justice. Hence Christ often says in the Gospel: [[Matt 9:22|thy faith hath made thee whole|Fides tua te salvum fecit]][[Luke 7:50||]]. [[3:22|Unto all, and upon all them that believe in him|In omnes et super omnes qui credunt in eum]], unto all Jews and upon all Gentiles, that is, in Christ, by formed faith, as is said in the Acts: [[Acts 13:39|In him every one that believeth is justified|In hoc omnis qui credit, justificatur]] [the margin gives Acts 10:43; the words are those of Acts 13:39]; and again: [[Acts 15:9|purifying their hearts by faith|fide purificans corda eorum]]. [[3:22|For there is no distinction|Non enim est distinctio]] between Jew and Greek in the time of the law of the Gospel, as regards the justification spoken of, since [[Acts 10:34|God is not a respecter of persons|non est personarum acceptor Deus]]. And as the Saviour said: [[Mark 16:16|He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved|Qui crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit]].

paras.t: Omnes enim prædicti peccaverunt: et ergo non propriis meritis, sed gratia Dei justificantur, suntque consimiles in peccato ac spirituali inopia, sicut subjungitur, et egent gloria Dei, hoc est miseratione divina, videlicet gratia, per quam Deus gloriosus apparet: qui ex sua liberrima bonitate salvat electos, ita ut nullus in se ipso valeat gloriari, sed omne bonum Domino adscribatur. Justificati ab injustitia culpæ, gratis, sine præcedentibus meritis, per gratiam ipsius Dei, quæ est causa formalis nostræ justificationis, sicut albedo est causa formalis albefactionis parietis, per redemptionem quæ est in Christo Jesu, id est per passionem et sanguinem Christi, in quo est redemptio nostra sicut in causa efficiente, ita quod passio ejus est causa instrumentalis effectiva ac meritoria nostræ salvationis. Unde de eo scriptum est: Qui dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo. Et Isaias ait: Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum; et Ipse peccata multorum tulit.
paras.en: [[3:23|For all have sinned|Omnes enim prædicti peccaverunt]], all those spoken of: and so they are justified not by their own merits but by the grace of God, and are alike in sin and spiritual poverty, as is added: [[3:23|and do need the glory of God|et egent gloria Dei]], that is, the divine compassion, namely grace, through which God appears glorious: who of his most free goodness saves the elect, so that no one can glory in himself, but all good is ascribed to the Lord. [[3:24|Being justified|Justificati]] from the injustice of guilt, [[3:24|freely|gratis]], without preceding merits, [[3:24|by his grace|per gratiam ipsius]], God's, which is the formal cause of our justification, as whiteness is the formal cause of the whitening of a wall, [[3:24|through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus|per redemptionem quæ est in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the Passion and blood of Christ, in whom our redemption is as in its efficient cause, so that his Passion is the instrumental, effective and meritorious cause of our salvation. Hence it is written of him: [[Apoc 1:5|who hath loved us and washed us from our sins in his own blood|Qui dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo]]. And Isaias says: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]; and: [[Is 53:12|he hath borne the sins of many|Ipse peccata multorum tulit]].

paras.t: Quem, videlicet Christum, proposuit, id est, nobis manifeste exhibuit, Deus Pater seu Trinitas, propitiatorem, id est reconciliatorem ac mediatorem, per fidem, mediante qua consequimur fructum dominicæ passionis, seu gratiam Dei. […] ipsius, id est merito effusionis sanguinis Christi. Unde in Isaia propheta scriptum est: Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Et Joannes ait: Advocatum habemus apud Patrem, Jesum Christum justum: et ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris. Sic autem Deus proposuit Christum propitiatorem finaliter, ad ostensionem justitiæ suæ, id est, quatenus se justum manifestaret, implendo sua promissa, nec deserendo peccata impunita, imo in Christo quodammodo vindicans ea, quemadmodum Isaias ait: Propter scelus populi mei percussi eum; et Christus in Psalmo, Quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam. Proposuit quoque sic Christum propitiatorem ex parte nostri, propter remissionem præcedentium delictorum, id est peccatorum quæ Christi adventum præcesserunt. Vel, Propter remissionem delictorum præcedentium, id est hominum qui ante Christi incarnationem fuerunt, et tenebantur in limbo inferni propter reatum originalis peccati. Per Christi vero passionem redempti atque educti sunt, juxta illud Zachariæ: Tu quoque, in sanguine testamenti tui, emisisti vinctos tuos de lacu in quo non est aqua. Delictorum, inquam, existentium in sustentatione, id est in pia atque longanimi patientia, Dei, qui non statim ultus est ea, sed clementer ignovit; vel, Præcedentium hominum existentium in sustentatione Dei, qui eos in limbo sustentavit ac conservavit sine pœna sensus.
paras.en: [[3:25|Whom|Quem]], namely Christ, [[3:25|God hath proposed|proposuit Deus]], that is, has plainly shown to us, God the Father, or the Trinity, [[3:25|to be a propitiation|propitiatorem]], that is, a reconciler and mediator, [[3:25|through faith|per fidem]], by means of which we obtain the fruit of the Lord's Passion, or the grace of God. […] [the words *in his blood* are missing from the transcription] his, that is, by the merit of the shedding of Christ's blood. Hence it is written in Isaias the prophet: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]. And John says: [[1 John 2:1|we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the just|Advocatum habemus apud Patrem, Jesum Christum justum]]: [[1 John 2:2|And he is the propitiation for our sins|et ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris]]. And God proposed Christ as propitiation in this way as to the end, [[3:25|to the shewing of his justice|ad ostensionem justitiæ suæ]], that is, so as to show himself just, fulfilling his promises and not leaving sins unpunished, but in a manner avenging them in Christ, as Isaias says: [[Is 53:8|for the wickedness of my people have I struck him|Propter scelus populi mei percussi eum]]; and Christ in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:5|then did I pay that which I took not away|Quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam]]. He proposed Christ as propitiation in this way also on our side, [[3:25|for the remission of former sins|propter remissionem præcedentium delictorum]], that is, of the sins that went before Christ's coming. Or, *for the remission of former sins*, that is, of the men who were before Christ's incarnation and were held in the limbo of hell for the guilt of original sin. But through Christ's Passion they were redeemed and led out, according to that word of Zacharias: [[Zach 9:11|Thou also by the blood of thy testament hast sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit, wherein is no water|Tu quoque, in sanguine testamenti tui, emisisti vinctos tuos de lacu in quo non est aqua]]. Of sins, I say, that were [[3:26|Through the forbearance of God|in sustentatione Dei]], that is, in the loving and long-suffering patience of God, who did not at once avenge them but mercifully pardoned; or, of the men who went before, being in the forbearance of God, who upheld and preserved them in limbo without the pain of sense.

paras.t: Utramque vero sustentationem Deus exhibuit ad ostensionem justitiæ ejus, id est propriæ æquitatis vel justitiæ, quam causat in nobis in hoc tempore evangelicæ legis, ut sit ipse Deus justus in operibus suis, et a Christianis justus cognoscatur, tanquam auctor justitiæ nostræ. […] Christi, id est quemcumque in Christum credentem, qui in Deo renatus et spiritualis effectus est virtute fidei, non justitia legis.
paras.en: God showed both these kinds of forbearance [[3:26|for the shewing of his justice|ad ostensionem justitiæ ejus]], that is, of his own equity or justice, which he causes in us [[3:26|in this time|in hoc tempore]] of the law of the Gospel, [[3:26|that he himself may be just|ut sit ipse justus]], God, in his works, and may be known by Christians to be just, as the author of our justice. […] [the words *and the justifier of him who is of the faith of Jesus* are missing from the transcription] Christ, that is, of whoever believes in Christ, who has been born again in God and made spiritual by the power of faith, not by the justice of the law.

paras.t: Ex præinductis ostendit Apostolus vanitatem jactantiæ Judæorum. Ubi est ergo gloriatio tua, o Judæe? id est, quoniam Deus proposuit Christum propitiatorem per fidem ad ostensionem seu manifestationem suæ justitiæ (secundum intelligentiam præinductam), ubi jam est, o Judæe, vana gloriatio tua, qua de justitia legis præsumens, te gentibus præferebas, easque spernebas, et sine lege tua eas non posse salvari putabas? Exclusa, id est ablata, est gloriatio ista. Per quam legem? An per legem factorum, id est per legem Mosaicam? Non utique: illa enim non salvavit per se; sed per legem fidei, id est per legem evangelicam, quæ salvat per fidem sine operibus legis. Appellatur autem lex Moysis, lex factorum, præsertim quantum ad præcepta cæremonialia. Sic quippe erat jugum gravissimum, laboriosissimis atque innumeris observantiis plenum. De quo Petrus in persona fidelium Judæorum loquens, testatur: Quod neque nos neque patres nostri portare potuimus. Secundum Augustinum autem, lex Moysis dicitur, factorum, quia minando imperabat, sed gratiam faciendi non præstabat. Lex vero evangelica vocatur lex fidei, quoniam opera mandat, et credendo gratiam faciendi acquirit.
paras.en: From what has been brought forward the Apostle shows the vanity of the Jews' boasting. [[3:27|Where is then thy boasting?|Ubi est ergo gloriatio tua?]] O Jew; that is, since God has proposed Christ as propitiation through faith, to the shewing or manifesting of his justice (in the sense brought forward), where now, O Jew, is your vain boasting, by which, presuming on the justice of the law, you set yourself above the Gentiles, and despised them, and thought that they could not be saved without your law? [[3:27|It is excluded|Exclusa est]], that is, taken away, this boasting. [[3:27|By what law?|Per quam legem?]] By the law [[3:27|Of works?|factorum?]] that is, by the law of Moses? [[3:27|No|Non]], certainly: for that did not save of itself; [[3:27|but by the law of faith|sed per legem fidei]], that is, by the law of the Gospel, which saves by faith without the works of the law. Now the law of Moses is called the law of works, especially as regards the ceremonial precepts. For so it was a most heavy yoke, full of most laborious and countless observances. Of which Peter, speaking in the person of the faithful Jews, testifies: [[Acts 15:10|which neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear|Quod neque nos neque patres nostri portare potuimus]]. But according to Augustine the law of Moses is called the law of works because it commanded by threatening, but did not give the grace of doing. The law of the Gospel, on the other hand, is called the law of faith, since it commands works and by believing obtains the grace of doing them.

paras.t: Arbitramur enim nos Apostoli, a Spiritu Sancto instructi, hominem quemcumque in Christum credentem, justificari per fidem caritate formatam, sine operibus legis cæremonialibus ac judicialibus. Triplicia namque erant præcepta veteris Testamenti, videlicet moralia, judicialia, cæremonialia. Præcepta autem cæremonialia, quoniam figurativa erant et pro statu illo solum accommoda, cessaverunt veritate veniente ac reserata, id est Christo passo ac prædicato. Judicialia vero præcepta sicut sine periculo in novo Testamento omittuntur (dummodo a nullo christiano prælato seu principe auctoritatem instituendi habente præcipiantur), sic sine periculo observantur, si a superiori instituantur, et Christianorum regimini congruant. Non enim solum figuralia exstiterunt. Præcepta autem moralia, quæ ordinantur ad bonos mores, et de actibus virtutum immediate donantur, non solum manent in novo Testamento, sed etiam per evangelica Christi consilia perficiuntur, et ad salutem requiruntur, juxta illud Matthæi: Si vis ingredi ad vitam, serva mandata.
paras.en: [[3:28|For we account|Arbitramur enim]], we Apostles, instructed by the Holy Ghost, [[3:28|a man|hominem]], any man who believes in Christ, [[3:28|to be justified by faith|justificari per fidem]] formed by charity, [[3:28|without the works of the law|sine operibus legis]], the ceremonial and judicial ones. For the precepts of the Old Testament were of three kinds, namely moral, judicial and ceremonial. The ceremonial precepts, since they were figurative and suited only to that state, ceased when the truth came and was laid open, that is, when Christ had suffered and been preached. The judicial precepts, as they are omitted in the New Testament without danger (provided they are not commanded by any Christian prelate or prince having authority to institute them), so they are observed without danger if they are instituted by a superior and suit the government of Christians. For they were not merely figurative. But the moral precepts, which are ordered to good conduct and are given immediately about acts of the virtues, not only remain in the New Testament but are also perfected by the Gospel counsels of Christ, and are required for salvation, according to that word of Matthew: [[Matt 19:17|if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments|Si vis ingredi ad vitam, serva mandata]].

paras.t: Denique hominem justificari sine operibus legis per fidem, declarat Apostolus. An Judæorum Deus tantum? id est, numquid Judæorum dumtaxat est Deus creator et salus, principium et finis? Nonne et gentium ipse creator et Deus est? Imo et gentium. Sicut ergo omnium Deus est, sic omnes uno modo justificat, puta per fidem. Et sicut omnes processerunt ab ipso, sic omnes reducuntur et convertuntur ad ipsum, per unum atque eumdem propitiatorem ac mediatorem Dei et hominum Jesum Christum. Ideo subditur: Quoniam quidem unus est Deus qui justificat circumcisionem, id est Judæos circumcisos, ex fide Salvatoris, hoc est per fidem de Christo, et qui justificat præputium, id est incircumcisos gentiles, per fidem eamdem. Eadem enim fides est fidelium novi ac veteris Testamenti, quamvis tempora sint mutata, et fides sit modo magis explicita. Quod equidem illi credebant futurum, nos credimus factum. Ipse quoque habitus fidei (quæ est virtus theologica) est unus in specie in omnibus fidelibus qui unquam fuerunt, sunt et erunt, propter formalem unitatem objecti, quod est veritas prima, propter quod credimus omnibus quæ cadunt sub fide. Patet ergo quia id quod ait, Ex fide et per fidem, sit idem in re, quamvis in ipso modo loquendi videatur distinctio. Apostolus namque frequenter mutat præpositiones et modum locutionis in eodem sensu.
paras.en: Lastly, the Apostle makes plain that man is justified by faith without the works of the law. [[3:29|Is he the God of the Jews only?|An Judæorum Deus tantum?]] that is, is God the creator and salvation, the beginning and end, of the Jews alone? [[3:29|Is he not also of the Gentiles?|Nonne et gentium?]] creator and God himself? [[3:29|yes, of the Gentiles also|Imo et gentium]]. As, then, he is the God of all, so he justifies all in one way, namely by faith. And as all came forth from him, so all are led back and turned to him through one and the same propitiator and [[1 Tim 2:5|mediator of God and men|mediatorem Dei et hominum]], Jesus Christ. Therefore there follows: [[3:30|For it is one God that justifieth circumcision|Quoniam quidem unus est Deus qui justificat circumcisionem]], that is, the circumcised Jews, [[3:30|by faith|ex fide]] in the Saviour, that is, by faith about Christ, [[3:30|and uncircumcision|et qui justificat præputium]], he who justifies the uncircumcised, that is, the Gentiles, [[3:30|through faith|per fidem]], the same faith. For the faith of the faithful of the New and of the Old Testament is the same, though the times have changed and faith is now more explicit. For what they believed would come, we believe has been done. And the very habit of faith (which is a theological virtue) is one in kind in all the faithful who ever were, are and will be, because of the formal unity of its object, which is the first truth, on account of which we believe all things that fall under faith. It is plain, then, that what he says, *by faith* and *through faith*, is the same in reality, though in the very manner of speaking there seems to be a distinction. For the Apostle often changes prepositions and the manner of speech in the same sense.

paras.t: Quoniam vero ex prædictis atque similibus verbis imponebant Judæi Paulo, quod esset legis destructor, propterea se excusans, adjecit: Legem ergo Mosaicam destruimus per fidem et Evangelium, ut nobis imponitur? Absit. Sed legem statuimus, id est, approbamus ac roboramus pro statu ac tempore. Quum ergo lex vetus fuerit via ac dispositio ordinata ad evangelicam legem, non dicitur destrui, sed impleri ac perfici evangelica lege superveniente: cessat tamen, quantum ad modum prioris observantiæ. Unde Ambrosius dicit: Non destruitur lex, quum impleta secundum spiritum, cessat secundum litteram: quia hic, scilicet in novo Testamento, gratia fidei est qua impletur lex, quæ sine fide esset infirma. Firmatur equidem lex, quoniam cærimonialia spiritualiter implentur; et quod minus in moralibus continebat, in Evangelio additur; et quod tunc promittebatur futurum, fides advenisse testatur. Tollitur autem littera occidens, et moralia litteraliter manent ac perficiuntur. Propter quod ait Salvator: Non veni solvere legem, sed adimplere.
paras.en: But since, from these and similar words, the Jews charged Paul with being a destroyer of the law, he excuses himself and adds: [[3:31|Do we then, destroy the law through faith?|Legem ergo destruimus per fidem?]] the law of Moses, through faith and the Gospel, as is laid to our charge? [[3:31|God forbid! But we establish the law|Absit. Sed legem statuimus]], that is, we approve and strengthen it, for its state and time. Since, then, the old law was a way and a preparation ordered to the law of the Gospel, it is not said to be destroyed but to be fulfilled and perfected when the law of the Gospel comes after it: yet it ceases as to the manner of its former observance. Hence Ambrose says: The law is not destroyed when, being fulfilled according to the spirit, it ceases according to the letter: for here, namely in the New Testament, there is the grace of faith by which the law is fulfilled, which without faith would be weak. The law is indeed made firm, since the ceremonies are fulfilled spiritually; and what it lacked in its moral precepts is added in the Gospel; and what was then promised as to come, faith testifies has come. But [[2 Cor 3:6|the letter killeth|littera occidens]] [Denis: "the killing letter"] is taken away, and the moral precepts remain according to the letter and are perfected. For which reason the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:17|I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil|Non veni solvere legem, sed adimplere]] [Denis: "I am not come to destroy the law"].

4.title: Explanatio capituli quarti: Quid ergo dicemus invenisse Abraham?
